name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II (BASS-II)

sources.note: PSI-25 flightProgram 'International Space Station (ISS)'; tests run in the Microgravity Science Glovebox aboard the ISS
Challenge brief lists BASS-II among microgravity combustion studies on the ISS

objective.value: Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread and extinction limits of solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity; begin to bridge the gap between the normal-gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 screening method and actual microgravity material flammability (including thicker fuels as rods, slabs and spherical sections); and feed combustion models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in space and on Earth.

sources.note: PSI-25 'objective' field: four stated objectives (flame spread/extinction limits in low-velocity forced flow, bridging the NASA-STD-6001 gap, providing SoFIE data, and testing thicker fuels)
PSI-25 SubResearch Area 'Spacecraft Fire Safety' and the investigation name includes 'Suppression'; objective cites fire detection and suppression system design
Challenge brief: flammability studies of solids such as fabrics and plastics (BASS, BASS-II) support prevention / material selection

safety_functions.note: Suppression from the name and the nitrogen-suppressant tests; prevention from the flammability-limit / material-selection framing.

sources.note: PSI-25 tests solid fuels (PMMA, SIBAL fabric, Nomex, wax candle) in forced flow

value: polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) - films, rods, slabs and a spherical section

sources.note: PSI-25 experimental table (data/source/psi/tables/PSI-25.csv) fuel-sample column: PMMA films 0.1-5 mm, clear/black PMMA rods, 4 cm spherical section, SIBAL sheets, Nomex natural (Nomex III), Japan wax candle

fuel_geometry.value: Films/flat sheets (1-2 cm wide, ~0.1-5 mm thick); cylindrical PMMA rods (1/4 to 1/2 inch diameter, clear and black); a 4 cm spherical section; PMMA slabs; and SIBAL fabric sheets.

sources.note: PSI-25 objectives list slabs, cylinders and spherical sections; the per-test table gives the actual sample geometries and widths
PSI-25 experimentHardware 'Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)'; tests run inside the sealed MSG work volume

apparatus.value: Small fan-driven flow duct / wind tunnel (modified SPICE hardware) with an igniter and a nitrogen injection nozzle; samples mounted in the duct.

sources.note: PSI-25 approach: fuel samples mounted inside a small wind tunnel in the MSG that could impose airflow up to 40 cm/s
Challenge brief 'Hardware': BASS/BASS-II used the modular fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE inside the MSG
PSI PSI-25 experimental table PSI-25_Experimental table_BASS-II.csv; per-test conditions, min and max of the listed columns

o2_percent.note: Range over 129 test rows of PSI-25_Experimental table_BASS-II.csv, columns: Calibrated  initial O2 % by vol. Computed by scripts/psi_table_summary.py (initial conditions only).

pressure_psi.note: No readable source states a pressure for BASS-II tests: the PSI per-test table has no pressure column and the BASS overview PDF gives no pressure. Left unknown rather than inferred.

sources.note: PSI-25 approach: the small wind tunnel 'could impose airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s'
BASS/BASS-II SIBAL fabric paper: flow speed varied from 40 cm/s down to 1 cm/s in the duct

airflow.note: Recorded 1-40 cm/s (SIBAL fabric tests and the 40 cm/s tunnel limit). The BASS overview PDF instead gives a crew-adjustable 5-50 cm/s for the BASS family, so confidence is medium (see review.notes).

sources.note: PSI-25 Project Type is 'Microgravity Investigation'
Challenge brief frames BASS-II as a low-gravity (microgravity) combustion study aboard the ISS

gravity_g.note: PSI Project Type states microgravity; recorded as ~0 g.

sources.note: PSI-25 objective: 'Ambient oxygen concentration (via working volume nitrogen vitiation)'; approach: oxygen varied below 21% by adding nitrogen

diluents.note: Nitrogen is the vitiating gas used to lower oxygen; nitrogen was also injected below the sample as the fire suppressant.

value: Forced flow velocity (speed and direction: concurrent vs opposed flow)
Ambient oxygen concentration (lowered by working-volume nitrogen vitiation)
Fuel sample geometry and material (films, rods, slabs, spherical section, fabrics)
Fuel thickness (about 0.1 mm to 5 mm PMMA)

sources.note: PSI-25 objective lists the primary variables: forced flow velocity (speed and direction), ambient oxygen concentration, and sample geometry; approach names airflow speed and oxygen as the main variables

value: Oxygen mole fraction held roughly constant within a test run while flow speed was varied

sources.note: PSI-25 hypothesis: 'Testing at constant O2 mole fractions permits studying flame spread and extinction at low and high flow speed'

held_constant.note: PSI states the varied variables explicitly but does not enumerate the constants; only the constant-O2-within-a-test point is directly supported.

value: Video camera (flame imaging, concurrent and second views)
On-board combustion-product gas sensors (CSA-CP and CDM: CO/CO2)

sources.note: PSI-25 per-test table has a 'Radiometer gain' column; the file list shows raw video and still-sequence files; PSI publication list includes a paper on CSA-CP and CDM sensor readings during BASS-II
BASS overview (covers BASS, BASS-II, BASS-M): an anemometer measures flow, a radiometer measures flame output, and video/still cameras record each test

sensors.note: Radiometer and combustion-product sensors are BASS-II-specific; the anemometer and cameras come from the family-level BASS document.

relevance_notes.value: BASS-II is a solid-fuel flammability and suppression study in low-velocity forced flow in microgravity, directly relevant to fire prevention (material selection and flame-spread/extinction limits) and suppression in crewed spacecraft. PSI lists it under Combustion Science / Spacecraft Fire Safety, and the brief names BASS and BASS-II as the solid-material flammability studies for prevention.

sources.note: PSI-25 SubResearch Area 'Spacecraft Fire Safety'; objectives cover solid-fuel flame spread and extinction limits and fire detection/suppression models
Challenge brief 'Background': flammability studies focus on solid materials such as fabrics and plastics (BASS and BASS-II)

value: Validated microgravity combustion models are used to build more complex models for flames in normal gravity, applicable to wildfires, building fires, waste-to-energy combustion and other terrestrial combustion problems
Improved selection of safe materials and improved firefighting methods

sources.note: PSI-25 'Research Impacts/Earth Benefits': models can be used to study flames on Earth such as wildfires, building fires and energy recapture from waste recycling; BASS-II helps engineers select safer materials and improve firefighting methods
